text: The Vietnam-Chile Business Forum held in Hanoi

The Vietnam-Chile Business Forum was held in Hanoi on November 16, 2026, as part of Chilean President José Antonio Kast's official visit to Vietnam, bringing together business communities from both countries to explore new trade and investment opportunities.

Organised by the Vietnam Chamber of Commerce and Industry (VCCI) in coordination with Chile's Export Promotion Bureau (ProChile), the forum coincided with the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.

Speaking at the event, VCCI Deputy Secretary-General Tran Ngoc Liem said President Kast's visit and participation in the forum demonstrated Chile's strong commitment to strengthening bilateral economic, trade and investment ties.

Vietnam and Chile have significant opportunities to expand cooperation under the Vietnam-Chile Free Trade Agreement (VCFTA), which took effect in 2014, and the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), of which both countries are members.
Bilateral trade exceeded $1.6 billion in the first 10 months of 2026, up 4.3% year-on-year.
Chilean exports to Vietnam reached more than $354 million, representing a 23% increase.

Ms. Susana Jiménez, President of the Confederation of Production and Commerce of Chile (CPC), highlighted Asia's growing importance, accounting for 55% of Chile's total exports in 2025, worth nearly $60 billion.
She described Vietnam as an attractive market, citing its population of more than 100 million, dynamic economy and growing integration into global supply chains.
Vietnam has become Chile's third-largest import source in Asia.
Addressing the forum, President Kast called on businesses to strengthen bilateral investment, particularly by promoting partnerships among small and medium-sized enterprises and start-ups.
